validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: Real proposal, independently corroborated. Origin is Turkish Energy Minister Alparslan Bayraktar's April 2025 S&P Global interview announcing plans for new gas AND crude export pipelines from Iraq (Basra) to Ceyhan via Haditha/Silopi (reported by Turkiye Today and Hellenic Shipping News, both tracing to that S&P interview). Independent later reporting confirms the corridor is live and advancing: The National (2026-03-16), MEES (2026-04-24, 'Hormuz Crisis Revives Basra-Ceyhan Pipeline Push'), Iraq Business News (2026-04-27, 'proposal back under consideration'), AGBI (2026-05), FDD (2026-05). Not a GEM-only/phantom entity. CLASSIFICATION: The Basra-Ceyhan corridor is primarily an OIL project ($5bn, ~$1.5bn allocated by PM Sudani in April 2026; ~650 km Turkish section, 40 and 46-inch pipes, ~1.5 mb/d). Natural gas transmission is explicitly named as part of the same integration plan ('the project would encompass natural gas transmission') and Turkey's short-term intent is to supply gas to Iraq for power generation, later reversing to export Iraqi gas. So recording the gas element as a distinct proposed transmission line is defensible, but it is the thinnest-specified component of a multi-commodity corridor. DUPLICATE: Within the 16-pipeline Iraq gas roster there is no duplicate (no other Basra->Ceyhan/Adana row). Any oil counterpart would live in GOIT, not this gas set. ATTRIBUTION/ENDPOINTS: Start=Basra, End=Ceyhan terminal (Adana), Türkiye, transiting Haditha and Silopi -- consistent with all sources. Fuel=Gas and PipelineType=transmission are correct for the gas component. ProposalYear=2025 matches the April 2025 announcement.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Status remains 'proposed' with abundant fresh independent evidence -- not stale, not advanced to construction/FID. The Basra-Ceyhan/Development Road corridor is still in negotiation/planning as of mid-2026: The National (2026-03) reports Iraq working to revive the Turkey route; MEES (2026-04-24) and Iraq Business News (2026-04-27) report the proposal 'back under consideration' amid the Hormuz crisis; AGBI (2026-05) reports Iraq's cabinet approved ~$1.5bn toward the ~$5bn Basra-Haditha-Turkey project but explicitly notes no FID/construction; Turkish Minute (2026-07-04) reports Iraq and Turkey still negotiating a temporary protocol as the existing Kirkuk-Ceyhan deal nears its 27 July expiration. The cabinet money and Chinese-partnership talk concern the OIL corridor; the gas line specifically has no groundbreaking or FID. Under dormancy rules this is well within thresholds and actively progressing on paper, so no presumed downgrade. Verdict: confirm 'proposed', evidence_date 2026-07.
